This user experience seems very half finished in the apps development and the app needs improvement, perhaps in the next OS.

title: Lack of User Experience Customization
body:
I genuinely enjoy the workouts and the coaching quality on Apple Fitness+. The trainers are engaging, the content is motivating, and the overall concept is excellent. However, the user experience — especially around customization — needs significant improvement.

The biggest issue is the lack of true editing within Custom Plans. If I want to make even small adjustments, I often have to rebuild the entire plan from scratch instead of simply modifying existing settings. This makes it unnecessarily time-consuming and discourages flexibility as my schedule or fitness needs change.

The “swap” feature is also very limited. Instead of allowing users to freely swap in any workout that fits their needs, the app only allows selections from a restricted list. This reduces personalization and makes it harder to adapt workouts to real-life preferences or goals.

Another usability challenge is equipment selection when creating schedules. Currently, it feels too restrictive — for example, I may want workouts that combine both mat work and dumbbells so I can alternate between standing exercises and floor work for recovery or muscle balance. The current options don’t reflect how many people actually train, and it limits creativity and practicality.

Overall, the workouts themselves are great, but the customization tools and interface feel rigid and not very user-friendly. Improving flexibility, editing capabilities, and equipment filtering would significantly enhance the experience.

title: Some advanced notice????
body:
I have used this app for a few years now and have recommended it to many people because of the varied workout types and a vast selection. I would give this a five star rating if not for one thing… vanishing workouts. 

I had workouts that I added to my library (which, I would have thought would act like a storage space rather than a directory). Some of these I did regularly and others I liked and would return to on occasion. Recently, I discovered that some of my library workouts - including one that my chiropractor suggested I use as a good preventative maintenance for an earlier sustained injury - had vanished. Checking the workout sections showed that they were no longer listed anywhere. Cleaning up cloud storage space?

I understand that server maintenance will occasionally require that files be deleted but it would be nice if users could be notified that certain workouts are scheduled for removal. Perhaps even given the option to purchase, for a one-time fee, and download those files for local use as long as they maintain their subscription (maybe just 25 or 50 cents per selected file since we’re already paying for the subscription).  The code for this isn’t that complex and it would give users the opportunity to decide how much they really want a particular workout that is likely to be removed because the overall community isn’t using it as frequently as your analytics would like.

Just a thought.

I think the developers of this app should contemplate the harm they are doing by suggesting an impossible low number as the default. Eating disorders are real. Please be kind to yourselves!

I don’t typically do the ratings / reviews but I need better from the default apple fitness app that I didn’t ask to be downloaded on my phone.

title: Workouts great. App sucks.
body:
I love all of the instructors and the workouts are fun and challenging. However the app itself sucks. There is no reason why these issues shouldn’t have been fixed by now:
1. No fast forward or rewind. App crashes there is no way to resume a workout from where you are. Internet go out and have to pick up workout late. No way fast forward to where you were. Get interrupted. There’s no way to go back to where you were. Missed an instruction or want to view something again. No rewind. 
2.  Airplay to smart TV can be glitchy. If it crashes see note 1 - there’s no fast forward. 
3. SharePlay is glitchy. It’s not always synced and it doesn’t mute the sound for the other person so you’ll hear an echo of the workout. You both have to be on mute so then you can’t talk to each other. 
4.  There’s no way to use your laptop. For some reason they locked the app so it’s only on iphone, iPad or Apple TV. No idea why they wouldn’t do it for your laptop too since the screen is better and bigger.

body:

What a useless mess.  With my Garmin watch and using the free app, I can set several goals; steps, stairs climbed, and intensity minutes are the three I use daily.  I’m also able to track activity specific metrics across applications and add activity specific external sensors if I want.

Annnd with this app I can change my calorie goal!?!?

A metric extrapolated by a series of inferred assumptions is my goal?

Oh and all of that other data collected by my various other devices is where?  

Never mind that I can only get an accurate update on my “goals” by restarting my phone.  

Apple I expected better-and maybe if I had an Apple Watch it would be better, but after this introduction, the only way I’d try that is if I got one for free and started wearing it along with my Garmin

However, I have a chronic illness that requires me to do a steady amount each day, but to avoid overdoing it.  Over exerting myself is very bad for my condition. Instead, it is important that I pace myself and spread my activity as evenly as possible through the day.
I would adore it if my watch could help with that. 

I know that some of the health app features ask you about certain conditions and change the program accordingly. It would be wonderful to have an option in the Activity app to also be reminded to slow down and rest for those of us who need to prioritize it.

title: The app is perfect for me
body:

I have always wanted to try yoga, stepping into a yoga studio or gym is always a bit intimidating. I’ve been able to set realistic goals by starting with all of Jessica’s 10 minute Yoga classes then work through the 20 and 30 minute ones. I’m now feeling much stronger and more confident in my practice as I work through all of Jessica’s 45 minute Yoga classes. I’ve also enjoyed core workouts with Greg, and cycling with Tyrel. I connected with “Time to walk” during lockdowns to help with my mental fitness. Watching all the team mates work on Sign language is encouraging and I always mimic the screen. 
At this point of my review I feel like you have the understanding that this app has been beneficial for me. I hope it works for others too. The price is also perfect and integrates perfectly in our home. On the go is probably the toughest but I can download when need be.

title: Great, but could be better
body:
I love Fitness+! I honestly don’t think I’d be using it beyond my free trial… but here I am!

I love that the trainers focus on proper form for each movement and that it’s about making YOUR body stronger and not about what your body LOOKS like. 

A few things that I’d love to see in further development:

Ability to create weekly “playlists” - I often mix my exercises (e.g. 20 minutes of dance + 10 minutes of strength; 20 minutes of HIIT + 10 minutes of core, etc.). If I could create a weekly schedule where I could group the workouts I want in each day so that they could “auto play” by going right into the next workout as soon as the first is done… that would be amazing and save me some time each morning.
A pay scheme based on the workouts you want. I don’t use about 1/3 of the workouts on the app (treadmill, cycling, rowing, and meditation), yet I still have to pay to have access to all content. I wish I could pay based on the content I want, which would also make it easier to navigate through the workouts I actually use.
